column4: In this category, we list the notifications (i.e., user or trusted flagger reports) and sanctions (i.e., negative moderation decisions) that fall under our “Hateful content” policy. We define hateful content as any content containing hateful behavior or undermining human dignity, including attacks, insults, threats, or incitement to hatred, violence, or discrimination based on personal attributes real or supposed, such as: race, ethnicity, nationality, religion/faith/beliefs, caste, language, sexual orientation, sex/gender, gender identity, physical appearance, illness, disability, migratory status, and eating disorders, or more generally, fueling hatred by instilling discriminatory ideas and beliefs in people’s mind. Such hateful content may take the form of outrageous expression, terms of contempt, invectives, stereotyping, attempts to offend, stigmatization, dehumanization, declarations of inferiority, expressions of disgust, insults, marginalization, or provocations of hatred, violence, or discrimination against individuals or groups of individuals targeted because of their personal attributes or characteristics. It also includes content that legitimizes, trivializes, or denies the existence of genocide, war crimes, or crimes against humanity

In this category, we list the notifications (i.e., user or trusted flagger reports) and sanctions (i.e., negative moderation decisions) that fall under our  “Child Sexual Exploitation Material (CSEM)” policy. We define CSEM as any content that shows, describes, or otherwise represents a child (anyone under the age of 18) engaged in a real or simulated sexual act, or that is intended to exploit the child sexually. This specifically includes (1) Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) such as images, videos, or other media depicting the sexual abuse or assault of a child; (2) material that sexually depicts children in sexually suggestive ways, even if no physical abuse is shown; (3) content that has been manipulated or digitally created (including deepfakes or cartoons) to depict child sexual exploitation; and (4) any material that is used to groom, lure, or exploit children for sexual purposes.

column4: In this category, we list the notifications (i.e., user or trusted flagger reports) and sanctions (i.e., negative moderation decisions) that fall under our  “Misleading and/or spam” policy. We define misleading and spam content as any irrelevant, repetitive, misleading, or unsolicited content, often created to deceive, promote scams, or manipulate engagement metrics (such as views, likes, or clicks). This specifically includes (1) financial gain scams designed to defraud users; (2) tutorials on illegal access to content; (3) impersonation in video where bad actors misrepresent themselves as legitimate entities or individuals; (4) legitimate business promotional content that violates our policies on commercial spam; (5) low-quality videos created solely to manipulate platform algorithms; (6) misleading content and clickbait that deceives users about the actual content of videos; (7) phishing attempts aimed at stealing personal information or credentials; and (8) SEO spam designed to manipulate search rankings and visibility artificially.

column4: In this category, we list the notifications (i.e. user or trusted flagger reports) and sanctions (i.e. negative moderation decisions) that fall under our “Shocking, malicious, violent, or dangerous” policy. We define violence as any content and associated metadata that cause, threaten, encourage, or glorify harm toward individuals or groups. This includes (1) Cyberharassment: content that threatens, bullies, intimidates, stalks, or maliciously targets individuals or groups—including doxxing and coordinated harassment campaigns. (2) Exploitative content: (2.a) Human exploitation and trafficking, (2.b) Cult-related content: content that manipulates, coerces, or exploits vulnerable individuals or groups for ideological, psychological, or financial gain, including encouraging harmful or isolating behaviors. (2.b) Sexually exploitative content: Any content or visual depiction that is non-consensual, abusive, or exploitative, or content that objectifies, endangers, or violates the autonomy of any person. (3) Unauthorized violence: (3.a) Personal attacks: content that depicts, encourages, or incites violence, physical harm (including suicide, self-harm), or targeted abuse against individuals or groups. (3.b) Promotion of violence or vulgarity: content that depicts, glorifies, trivializes, or encourages violent acts, brutality, or excessive vulgarity in ways that degrade or endanger others. (3.c) Animal death and suffering. (4) Unsafe, non-compliant or prohibited products
